subject: Post-call: procurement & deployment path (Acme) - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: procurement & deployment path (Acme) - next steps

Thanks for the time today, Sarah — good conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Call recap:
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood for in-product LLM features (recommendations + chat) with PII-sensitive subset for payments flow.
- Preferred initial deployment: Hosted for fastest time-to-value; explore Dedicated for isolation; Private/on-prem considered for regulated scope later.
- Procurement: Acme typically purchases via PO (not card). Legal will need MSA + SOW.

Open asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm your procurement contact (name + email) and the internal timeline for PO/MSA review?
2) Are you interested in procuring via cloud marketplace (GCP/AWS marketplace) to speed purchase, or do you prefer direct contract?
3) Ballpark budget or committed spend range to evaluate commit vs on-demand pricing (even a range helps).
4) Any constraints for a pilot (data residency, retention, SOC2 evidence)?

I'll loop Aditya for pricing options and Dev for marketplace cadence / onboarding. I'll put together 2–3 packaging options (hosted on-demand, hosted commit, dedicated reserved).

Attachments: call recording (link below).

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0124

Recording: https://redwood.zoom.us/rec/abc123

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement & deployment path (Acme) - next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few answers from procurement/legal side: 

- Procurement contact: Tom Chen (tom.chen@acme.com) — he owns PO & vendor onboarding.
- Payment method: We will almost certainly use PO (card is rare at our scale).
- Paper process: Legal needs a Master Services Agreement + Statement of Work with clear data handling clauses.
- Marketplace: Yes — we prefer marketplace purchases where possible (makes approvals easier), but will consider direct contract if there are material discounts or custom terms.
- Pilot constraints: Pilot can be hosted (no PII in pilot env), but for production we will need either Dedicated with network isolation or Private if PII/PCI is in scope.
- Timeline: Procurement review starts 2 weeks from today; target to have PO in ~3–4 weeks depending on legal redlines.
- Ballpark budget: target ~$150k–$300k ARR for year-one purchase depending on deployment model and discounts.

I attached our vendor onboarding checklist and PO process summary for reference (acme_po_process.pdf).

Let me know if you want to set a short call with Tom next week — happy to introduce.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Platform Partnerships, Acme Corp
sarah.jenkins@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme procurement — packaging alignment (for quote)

Looping you both — Sarah confirmed PO + marketplace preference and provided Tom as procurement contact. Timeline: procurement review starts in ~2 weeks; target PO in 3–4 weeks. Ballpark budget 150k–300k ARR.

Recommend we prepare:
- Option A: Hosted on-demand (no commit) — flexible, higher unit price, fastest start.
- Option B: Hosted 12-month commit (monthly billing) — ~25–30% discount, includes prefix caching + basic SLA.
- Option C: Dedicated reserved (monthly commit) — for isolation, higher base price; include burst capacity details and SLA.
- Option D: Private (VPC / on-prem) — for long-term PII/PCI, longer onboarding, professional services + annual license.

Preliminary stance: Propose a pilot on Hosted (Option A or small commit B) with the option to convert to Dedicated once scope for PII is confirmed. Highlight marketplace procurement as lowering procurement friction; if marketplace is used, pricing/billing flows may differ (we should check marketplace discounting / revenue share).

Aditya — can you pull together a quick three-line quote (A/B/C) and attach a simplified pricing sheet (pricing_quick_quote_draft.xlsx)? Dev — can you confirm typical marketplace lead-times and whether we have a standard listing process for Acme's cloud (GCP/AWS)?

I will draft a short email template to introduce Tom and attach MSA + SOW examples.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme procurement — packaging alignment (for quote)

Thanks — attaching a quick draft. Notes below; full pricing sheet attached (pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx) and draft MSA redlines (MSA_redlines_acme.pdf).

High-level pricing options (ballpark):
- Option A (Hosted, on-demand): $0.014 / token-equivalent effective; estimated pilot cost (3 months, light usage) ~$8k–$15k.
- Option B (Hosted, 12-month commit): 25% discount off on-demand; commit bands: $100k, $200k, $300k with stepped pricing and reserved capacity boosts.
- Option C (Dedicated reserved): Monthly reserved capacity starting ~$18k/month (1 GPU pool), includes baseline SLA; professional services for onboarding ~$12k–$20k one-time.
- Option D (Private / on-prem): Custom pricing; typically higher one-time setup + annual license.

Marketplace note: If Acme purchases via AWS/GCP marketplace, settlement takes longer and our net to Redwood is lower (marketplace revenue share). We should present both direct and marketplace pricing, and include a note explaining procurement speed tradeoffs.

Action items:
- I'll finalize the pricing_quick_quote_draft.xlsx and pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx this afternoon.
- Marissa: please intro Tom and include: (1) preferred initial deployment (hosted vs commit), (2) procurement contact details, (3) expected signature timeline.
- Dev: confirm marketplace listing ETA and who from Partnerships owns the listing.

Attachments: pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx, MSA_redlines_acme.pdf

—
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
